> **The limits of self-reported data**
> 
> A great deal of what is known about diet comes from asking people what they eat. Participants complete a questionnaire, sometimes covering the previous year, and researchers convert their answers into estimates of calories and nutrients. The method is cheap and can cover very large samples, which is why it underlies a substantial proportion of nutritional research.
> 
> It is also unreliable. When self-reported intake is compared with objective measures such as doubly labelled water, which tracks energy expenditure directly, most participants appear to under-report consumption by between 20 and 30 per cent. Under-reporting is not random: it is markedly higher among people who are overweight, and higher among women than men.
> 
> This creates a problem that no amount of statistical adjustment fully solves. If the error correlates with the outcome being studied, findings can be distorted in ways that are difficult to detect. A study appearing to show that a particular diet is associated with lower weight may in part be showing that people who weigh less report their food more accurately.
> 
> Researchers are increasingly aware of the issue, and some journals now require studies to state clearly when conclusions rest on self-reported intake. Objective methods remain far too expensive for large populations, so the underlying difficulty has not gone away.

**True / False / Not Given (7–10):**
7. Self-reported dietary data is used in a large share of nutritional research.
8. Under-reporting occurs equally across all groups.
9. Doubly labelled water is cheaper than questionnaires.
10. Some journals now require studies to state when data is self-reported.

writing.de_tom_tat: Task 1, ≥150 từ: biểu đồ tròn về tỷ lệ chi tiêu hộ gia đình (nhà ở, thực phẩm, đi lại, giáo dục, khác).
writing.bai_mau:
The two pie charts illustrate how an average household divided its expenditure between five categories in 2000 and in 2020.

Overall, housing consumed a substantially larger share of household budgets by the end of the period, while the proportion spent on food fell markedly. Spending on education, by contrast, remained almost unchanged.

In 2000, food represented the single largest expense, accounting for 35 per cent of total spending. Housing came second at 25 per cent, followed by transport at 18 per cent. Education absorbed 12 per cent, with the remaining 10 per cent classified as other expenditure.

By 2020, the picture had altered considerably. Housing had risen to become the dominant category at 38 per cent, an increase of 13 percentage points. Food, meanwhile, had declined to just 22 per cent — a drop of well over a third in relative terms. Transport fell slightly to 15 per cent, whereas education edged up marginally from 12 to 13 per cent. Other expenditure showed the largest proportional rise, doubling from 10 to 12 per cent.

The clearest development is the reversal between housing and food, which exchanged first and second place over the twenty-year period.

cham_diem.vi_sao: So sánh hai biểu đồ tròn ở hai thời điểm — đúng yêu cầu. Nêu đủ 5 hạng mục ở cả hai mốc, Overview chỉ ra hai thay đổi lớn và một hạng mục không đổi.
Đoạn 3 tả năm 2000, đoạn 4 tả năm 2020 và so sánh trực tiếp. Từ nối thời gian và đối chiếu: By 2020 · meanwhile · whereas · by contrast.
Ngôn ngữ tỷ lệ: represented · accounting for · absorbed · classified as · the dominant category · in relative terms · edged up marginally · proportional rise.

Quá khứ hoàn thành (had altered, had risen, had declined) — đúng khi so mốc sau với mốc trước · mệnh đề rút gọn (accounting for, doubling from) · mệnh đề quan hệ (which exchanged first and second place).

dang_hoc: Biểu đồ tròn hai thời điểm thì phải so sánh, không tả rời từng cái. Dùng quá khứ hoàn thành cho mốc sau.
Bộ từ diễn đạt tỷ lệ cần thuộc: account for · represent · make up · constitute · absorb.
Phân biệt tuyệt đối và tương đối: từ 35% xuống 22% là giảm 13 điểm phần trăm, nhưng giảm hơn một phần ba in relative terms. Nêu được cả hai là dấu hiệu band cao.
"edged up marginally" cho thay đổi rất nhỏ — chính xác hơn "increased a little".
loi_thuong_gap: ❌ Tả riêng từng biểu đồ mà không so sánh → mất điểm Task Achievement.
❌ Cộng các phần không bằng 100% → luôn kiểm tra lại.
❌ Dùng "percentage" thay cho "percentage points" khi nói về mức thay đổi.
❌ Bỏ qua hạng mục nhỏ nhất → phải nêu đủ tất cả các phần.

speaking.de_tom_tat: Part 1 — Money & living costs: Have prices risen where you live? / Do you budget? / What is your biggest expense?

cau_tra_loi.hoi: Have prices risen where you live?
cau_tra_loi.mau: Considerably, especially rent. Over the past five years housing costs have gone up much faster than salaries, which makes saving difficult.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Nêu mốc thời gian cụ thể và so sánh hai chỉ số (costs vs salaries).

cau_tra_loi.mau: I do, though not in great detail. I set aside a fixed amount at the beginning of each month, because if I wait until the end there's nothing left.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: Câu điều kiện loại 1 giải thích lý do — tự nhiên và đúng ngữ pháp.

cau_tra_loi.mau: Rent, by a long way — it takes roughly a third of my income. Food comes second, but it's far more manageable.
cau_tra_loi.ghi_chu: "by a long way" là cụm nhấn mạnh tự nhiên. Có số liệu cụ thể (a third).

cham_diem.vi_sao: Trả lời có số liệu và so sánh.
considerably · set aside · by a long way · manageable.
have gone up much faster than · if I wait… there's nothing left.

meo_noi: Số liệu cụ thể ("a third of my income") làm câu trả lời đáng tin hơn hẳn.
"by a long way" = hơn hẳn — dùng để nhấn mạnh so sánh nhất.
